title: UIIC AO 2026
note: Reasoning has 30 questions in 17 minutes: one garbled puzzle set was removed.

items.q: Which of the following options provides the most accurate synonym for the word "dismissed" as highlighted in the passage?
items.x: "Dismissed" here means rejected (as not worth considering).

items.q: Which of the following options carries the same contextual meaning as the word "serving" as used in the passage?
items.x: "Serving" in the military = performing duties.

items.q:
Which of the following statements can be inferred from the passage?
I. The foreign radio broadcasts immediately convinced Mr. Song to defect within a few days of listening.
II. Mr. Song was aware that defecting from his country could lead to severe consequences for his family.
III. Mr. Song held a position of responsibility within the military that gave him free access to cross borders legally.
items.x: Only II: he had seen what happened to families of those who fled. I is wrong (it took months), III is never stated.

items.q:
Based on the passage, which of the following factors contributed to Mr. Song’s successful crossing of the border?
I. He mentally planned his route across the frozen terrain prior to his departure.
II. He received financial and navigational assistance from foreign agents stationed at the border.
III. He chose to cross on foot during the winter season.
items.x: He mapped the frozen terrain beforehand (I) and crossed on foot in winter (III). No foreign help is mentioned.

items.q: Why did Mr. Song maintain a quiet and compliant demeanor while serving in the North Korean military?
o: He was deeply devoted to political ideologies taught in mandatory training sessions.
He was attempting to mislead his fellow soldiers while gathering secret information.
He hoped to gain a high-ranking position that would allow him to travel overseas.
He realized early on that avoiding unwanted attention was crucial for his survival.
He wanted to earn special privileges and official recognitions from the government.
items.x: He learned early that survival depended on never drawing unwanted attention.

items.q: What primary realization led Mr. Song to question the beliefs he had held since childhood?
o: The severe physical hardships he experienced while serving in military barracks.
The sudden enforcement of harsher political compliance rules by military officers.
The stark contrast between local reality and news heard on foreign radio programs.
The direct influence and persuasion of family members who had already defected.
The realization that his position in the military offered no financial stability.
items.x: The contrast between the radio's world and the reality he saw was too vast to dismiss.

items.q: Which of the following best describes the psychological turning point that drove Mr. Song to attempt escape?
o: Fear of arrest by military authorities surpassed his desire for personal freedom.
The weight of knowing the truth outweighed his fear of potential consequences.
A sudden opportunity presented itself during a night patrol that he seized quickly.
The unexpected loss of military rank forced him to seek shelter in China.
Complete inability to endure physical fatigue associated with army routine.
items.x: "The weight of what he now knew had become heavier than the fear of what might happen."

items.q: How did Mr. Song feel upon reaching China, despite facing language barriers and isolation?
o: Deeply regretful about abandoning his military position and social privilege.
Anxious that local police officers would repatriate him to his homeland.
Confident that he would instantly secure housing and employment opportunities.
Relieved that he no longer had to endure harsh physical winter conditions.
Overwhelmed by a novel sense of personal freedom he had never experienced.
items.x: He felt, for the first time, the overwhelming sensation of personal liberty.

items.q: Which of the following titles best captures the central theme of the passage?
o: The Harsh Realities of North Korean Military Training
Liberty Radio: The Foreign Broadcast Network Overseas
A Quiet, Deliberate Journey Toward Personal Freedom
Winter Operations Along the Chinese Border Patrol Route
Propaganda and Its Deep Psychological Impact on Officers
items.x: The passage follows his slow, deliberate journey to freedom.

items.q:
Choose the correct connector to adjoin the two sentences to form a grammatically correct sentence.
(I) The trainee followed instructions carefully during the complex account opening procedure.
(II) Errors were avoided despite multiple verification steps requiring close attention.
items.x: He followed instructions carefully; hence errors were avoided.

items.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (A)?
items.x: "Needs to become" — the others do not take a bare "to"-infinitive this way.

items.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (B)?
items.x: Overcrowding depletes (uses up) resources.

items.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (C)?
items.x: Tourism sustains families through jobs.

items.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (D)?
items.x: Carbon footprint.

items.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (E)?
items.x: Spending directly benefits the community.

items.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (F)?
items.x: Mishaps such as lost luggage.

items.q:
A word has been given in the question and used in the sentences below. Identify the statements where the word has been used in a contextually and grammatically correct manner. AMOUNT
(I) The total amount of money collected through donations was sufficient to support the relief campaign.
(II) The manager decided to amount the expenses before submitting the final financial report.
(III) Despite his limited resources, his hard work amounted to a significant improvement in the company's performance.
items.x: "Amount" as a noun (I) and "amounted to" (III) are correct; "amount the expenses" (II) is wrong.

items.q: The restorers were beneath (a) to discover that astonished (B) the layers of varnish lay an entirely different portrait (C).
items.x: The restorers were astonished to discover that beneath the layers of varnish lay an entirely different portrait.

items.q:
Moments after take-off, the pilot noticed a return (a) on the instrument panel and calmly flicker
(B) permission to requested (C) to the airport.
items.x: The pilot noticed a flicker on the instrument panel and calmly requested permission to return to the airport.

items.q: The treaty, which was signed in haste (A), sowed the erupt (B) of resentment that would eventually seeds (C) into another war.
items.x: The treaty, signed in haste, sowed the seeds of resentment that would eventually erupt into another war.

items.q: Astronomers detected faint atmosphere (a) of water vapour in the orbiting (B) of an exoplanet traces (C) a distant red dwarf.
items.x: Astronomers detected faint traces of water vapour in the atmosphere of an exoplanet orbiting a distant red dwarf.

items.q: The technician warned residents (A)/ they had better to dispose (B)/ of old batteries only at (C)/ the designated e-waste collection centre. (D)
items.x: "Had better" takes a bare infinitive: "had better dispose".

items.q: Not until the cycling (A)/ track project is completed (B)/ commuters will notice a real (C)/ reduction in peak-hour traffic congestion. (D)
items.x: "Not until …" at the start needs inversion: "will commuters notice".

items.q: Fishermen along the coast (A)/ said they were still (B)/ not familiar of the new (C)/ warning signals despite months of awareness campaigns. (D)
items.x: "Familiar with", not "familiar of".

items.q:
The counsellor asked the (A)/ trainee where did he want (B)/ to train further after completing
(C)/ the vocational programme this term. (D)
items.x: Reported question: "where he wanted to train".

items.q: Many a seasoned diver, having spent (A)/ years among the reefs, have admitted (B)/ that the sudden currents near the wreck (C)/ remain impossible to predict. (D)
items.x: "Many a" takes a singular verb: "has admitted".

items.q: In the question below, a part is highlighted in bold, which may not be grammatically correct. Choose the correct alternative for the highlighted part to make the sentence grammatically correct. You must **refrain from making personal comments** during formal discussions.
items.x: "Refrain from + -ing" is already correct.

items.q: In the question below, a part is highlighted in bold, which may not be grammatically correct. Choose the correct alternative for the highlighted part to make the sentence grammatically correct. Unless you **do not submit the documents**, your application will not be processed.
items.x: "Unless" already means "if not", so drop the "not": "Unless you submit the documents".

items.q: In the question below, a part is highlighted in bold, which may not be grammatically correct. Choose the correct alternative for the highlighted part to make the sentence grammatically correct. No sooner **did the bell rang than** the students rushed out of the classroom.
items.x: "No sooner did + base verb … than": "did the bell ring than".

items.q: In the question below, a part is highlighted in bold, which may not be grammatically correct. Choose the correct alternative for the highlighted part to make the sentence grammatically correct. She spoke **so soft that hardly anyone** could hear her speech.
items.x: The adverb "softly" modifies "spoke".

1-9.text: Read the following passage and answer the given questions. Mr. Song had spent seventeen years serving in the North Korean military, rising steadily through the ranks until he held a position that most men in his country would have considered a privilege. He wore his uniform with the discipline that the regime demanded, attended the mandatory political sessions without visible complaint, and performed every duty assigned to him with the quiet efficiency of a man who had learned very early in life that survival depended on never drawing unwanted attention. But beneath that carefully maintained surface, something had been changing for years. Late at night, when the barracks were silent, Mr. Song had been secretly tuning into Liberty Radio — a foreign broadcast that delivered news about the outside world in the Korean language. What he heard over those years could not be dismissed easily. The contrast between the world described on that radio and the reality he witnessed every day in his own country was too vast, too consistent, and too detailed to be explained away as enemy propaganda. He began to understand, slowly and reluctantly, that much of what he had been taught to believe since childhood was simply not true. The decision to leave did not come suddenly. It built over months of careful, silent calculation. Mr. Song knew the risks better than most — he had seen what happened to families of those who attempted to flee. But the weight of what he now knew had become heavier than the fear of what might happen if he tried. One winter night, he crossed the border into China on foot, moving through frozen terrain that he had mentally mapped over weeks of quiet preparation. The journey was brutal and uncertain, and there were moments when he was convinced, he would not survive it. He did survive. Exhausted and alone in a country whose language he did not speak, Mr. Song felt, for the first time in his adult life, something that his years of military service had never once offered him — the unfamiliar, overwhelming sensation of personal liberty.

11-16.text: In the following passage there are blanks, each of which has been denoted by a letter. For each blank, five options are given. Choose the most appropriate word from the options that fits the blank appropriately. Tourism has grown into one of the largest industries in the world, bringing both opportunities and challenges. Experts warn that responsible exploration ______________ (a) to become the norm rather than the exception. Overcrowding at popular beaches steadily ______________ (B) natural resources such as fresh water and clean sand. Yet the sector also ______________ (C) millions of families by providing jobs in hotels, transport, and handicrafts. Backpackers can reduce their carbon ______________ (D) by choosing railways over brief hops by air. Staying in locally owned guesthouses ensures that visitor spending directly ______________ (E) the community. Finally, an insurance policy protects holidaymakers from unexpected ______________ (F) like lost luggage or cancelled flights.

If more than one meaningful word can be formed, mark Y as your answer. If no meaningful word can be formed, mark X as your answer.
items.x: A, D, R, O form ROAD; its second letter is O.

items.q:
Study the following statements carefully. The statements establish certain relationships between different elements, followed by two conclusions. Based on the given statements, determine which of the conclusions logically follow and select the appropriate answer.
Statements: I ≥ J ≥ K = L; M < N ≤ L = O ≥ P
Conclusions:
I. J ≥ P II. M < J
o: If only conclusion I is true
If only conclusion II is true
If either conclusion I or II is true
If neither conclusion I nor II is true
If both conclusion I and II are true
items.x: J ≥ K = L = O ≥ P gives J ≥ P. M < N ≤ L = K ≤ J gives M < J.

items.q:
In this question, relationship between different elements is shown in the statements. These statements are followed by two conclusions. Assume the given statements to be true and find which of the given conclusions is true.
Statements: G = H < I; J ≥ I > K = L
Conclusions:
I. L < H
II. K ≥ G
o: If only conclusion I is true
If only conclusion II is true
If either conclusion I or II is true
If neither conclusion I nor II is true
If both conclusion I and II are true
items.x: L = K < I > H = G: no direct relation, but L < H and K ≥ G (= L ≥ H) together cover every case, so either follows.

items.q:
In this question, relationship between different elements is shown in the statements. These statements are followed by two conclusions. Assume the given statements to be true and find which of the given conclusions is true.
Statements: S ≥ T > V; W < V = X
Conclusions:
I. S > X
II. W < T
o: If only conclusion I is true
If only conclusion II is true
If either conclusion I or II is true
If neither conclusion I nor II is true
If both conclusion I and II are true
items.x: S ≥ T > V = X gives S > X. W < V < T gives W < T.

items.q: In the word ‘ HOLIDAY’, determine the number of pairs of letters such that the number of letters lying between them in the given word is exactly the same as the number of letters lying between them in the English alphabetical order (considering both forward and backward directions).
items.x: Only H and D: three letters (O, L, I) lie between them in HOLIDAY, and three (E, F, G) lie between them in the alphabet.

items.q:
Statements:
Only a few houses are wall No wall is painted All woods are houses
Conclusions:
I. Some houses are not painted
II. No woods being painted is a possibility
o: If either I or II follows
If neither I nor II follows
If both I and II follow
items.x: Some houses are walls and no wall is painted, so some houses are not painted. Woods may or may not be painted.

items.q:
Statements:
All Waterfalls are rivers. Only a few rivers are lakes. Only lakes are water.
Conclusions:
I. All Lakes can be Rivers.
II. Some Waterfalls can be Lakes.
o: Both conclusion I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
items.x: Some rivers are lakes, so all lakes being rivers is possible (I). Waterfalls and lakes are not linked, so some waterfalls can be lakes (II). Both follow. (The source key said only II.)

items.q:
In each question below some statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and
II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding commonly known facts. Give answer-
Statements:
Only a few refine is process All refine is products No factory is process
Conclusions:
I. All products can never be process
II. All refine being factory is a possibility
o: If either conclusion I or II follows
If neither conclusion I nor II follows
If both conclusions I and II follow
items.x: Some refine is process and all refine is products, so some products are process — I follows. Some refine is process and no factory is process, so all refine can never be factory — II fails.

items.q: In the number ‘75847361’ If 2 is subtracted from first four digits of the number and 1 is added to rest digit of the number, then, then how many digits will become prime digits?
items.x: New number 5 3 6 2 8 4 7 2: the prime digits are 5, 3, 2, 7, 2 = five.

31-35.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:
Eight persons, A to H, were born in different months of the same year from January to August, but not necessarily in the same order. C was born four months after H and immediately before A. C was born in the month having odd number of days. The number of persons were born before A is one more than the number of persons born after D. More than two persons were born between D and B. G was born immediately before E. F was born before E.
31-35.sol: Jan F · Feb D · Mar H · Apr G · May E · Jun B · Jul C · Aug A

37-40.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:
In a certain code language, 'Tiger is brave animal' is written as 'na mo ka so' 'Brave and smart lion' is coded as 'ka pa ri lu' 'Smart animal run fast' is coded as 'ri zo ja na' 'Lion and tiger run' is coded as 'lu pa mo ja'
37-40.sol: brave = ka, animal = na, tiger = mo, is = so, smart = ri, run = ja, fast = zo; and/lion = pa/lu (not fixed).

41-45.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:
Six persons, K, L, M, N, O and P, sit around a circular table, all facing inside. Each of them plays a different musical instrument: Guitar, Piano, Flute, Violin, Drums and Sitar. M is an immediate neighbour of O. The one who plays Flute sits second to the left of M. K sits third to the right of L, who is not an immediate neighbour of M. The one who plays Piano sits opposite the one who plays Sitar. P plays Guitar. N sits second to the right of the one who plays Drums. One of the immediate neighbours of O plays Sitar.
41-45.sol: Clockwise: K-Drums, M-Sitar, O-Violin, L-Flute, N-Piano, P-Guitar. All face the centre, so "right" is anticlockwise.

46-48.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:
There are eight members- K, G, J, H, D, L, P and R in a family of three generations. The family has two married couples. H is the son of K who is the father-in-law of D. L is the only son of D and the elder brother of P. J is the daughter of G, who is the grandmother of P. K has only one son. R is the sibling of L and P.
46-48.sol: K (male) and G are a couple with children H (son) and J (daughter). D is K's daughter-in-law, so D is married to H — or, reading "father-in-law" loosely, D could be J's husband. D's children: L (only son), P and R (daughters).

50-52.text:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:
An uncertain number of persons sit in a row and face north. H sits fifth to the right of B. D sits two places away from B. K sits third to the left of D. Four persons sit between M and K. M is not immediate neighbour of H. Only two persons sit to the left of M. Two persons sit between A and M. The number of persons sit between A and B is one more than number of persons sit between H and F. F sits to the left of H. Not more than two persons sit to the right of F.
50-52.sol: 14 persons, all facing north. From the left end (1st): M 3rd, A 6th, K 8th, B 9th, D 11th, F 12th, H 14th.

62-63.text: In the question below, some statements are given followed by two conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

items.q: What is the total number of students in section B across all five schools?
Section A of school R has what percent more students than section A of school S?
What is the average number of students in section A across all five schools?
Section B of school R is what percent of section A of school P?
If 20% of section B students in school S move to section A, what is the new ratio of A to B in school S?

P and Q started a business together. The investment of P is Rs 3000 more than that of Q. P’s capital remained invested for 8 months, while Q’s capital was invested for a year. If, at the end of the year, the total profit is Rs 9600, then find the investment (in Rs) of Q. (Note: The profit share of P is 24k, where k² + 625 = 40625.)
items.x: k² = 40000, k = 200, so P's share = 4800 = half the profit. P × 8 = Q × 12 with P = Q + 3000 gives Q = 6000.

items.q: A spends 18% of his income on food and clothing, 22% on transport, 40% of his daughter’s education and saves the remaining Rs.18600 in a month. What is the monthly income of A?
items.x: 18600 is 20% of income, so income = 93,000.

items.q: The average of four numbers A, B, C, and D is 20, and another number E is 10 more than the average of B and C. Find the value of 2E+A.
items.x: 2E + A = B + C + 20 + A = 80 − D + 20. D is unknown, so it cannot be determined.

items.q: The total number of products sold by all five shops in May is what percent of the total number of products sold by all five shops in June?
items.x: May total 1680, June total 2100: 80%.

items.q: In July, shop C sold 20% more products than it did in June, while shop E sold one-third fewer products than it did in June. What is the total number of products sold by shops C and E together in July?
What is the ratio of the total products sold by shops A and C together in May to the products sold by shop B in June?
The average number of products sold by shops A, B and E in June is how much more than the average number of products sold by the same three shops in May?
items.x: June average (420 + 480 + 450)/3 = 450; May average (360 + 420 + 240)/3 = 340; difference 110.

items.q: The number of products sold by shop E in June is what percent more than the number of products sold by shop C in May?
Suresh was married 14 yrs ago and his present age is 3/2 times of the age at the time of his marriage. If his son’s age is 1/3 rd of his father's present age, then find the age of his son.
items.x: 1.5x = x + 14 gives x = 28; Suresh is 42 and his son is 14.

items.q: A shopkeeper sells three identical items at a loss of 8%, a profit of 25% and a loss of 7% respectively. The average selling price of the three items is Rs. 1550. If the item is marked 20% above the cost price and sold at a discount of Rs. 150, what is the profit percentage?

B invests Rs Y in a scheme which offers 18% simple interest for four years and receives Rs.2880 as interest. If B invests Rs (Y+1500) in a bank which offers 20% compound interest for two years, then find the total amount received by B from the bank (in Rs).

A vessel contains 56 liters of milk and some water. If 24 liters of pure milk and 18 liters of water are added to the vessel, then the water in the new mixture becomes 20% of mixture. Find the initial quantity of water in the vessel?
items.x: (w + 18) = 0.2 × (98 + w) gives w = 2 litres.

items.q: Length of train P is 60 meters less than train Q. They cross a pole in 20 seconds and 15 seconds, respectively. If the speed of train Q is 72 km/h and the length of a bridge is half the length of train Q, then find the time taken by train P to cross the bridge.

The speed of the stream is 5 km/h, and the downstream speed of a ship is 10 km/h more than twice the speed of the stream. The ship sails from Port P to Port Q and returns back to Port P in 15 hours. The water flows from P to Q. Find the time taken (in hours) by the ship to cover twice the distance between P and Q in downstream.
items.x: Downstream 20, ship 15, upstream 10. D/20 + D/10 = 15 gives D = 100; 200/20 = 10 h.

items.q: The ratio of milk to water in a mixture is 5: 4. 90 liters of mixture are taken out and 30 liters water is added. Now, the quantity of milk in the mixture becomes 8 litres more than that of water. Find the initial quantity of mixture (in liters)?

Find the wrong number in the following number series. 12, 19, 48, 108, 232, 447, 789

96-100.text: Read the information carefully and answer the questions that follow. In a school of 600 students, each student studies English, Hindi, Sanskrit, some combination of them, or none, and one-sixth of the students study none of the three. 40 students study all three subjects, and the number who study only English and Hindi is 50% more than this. Students who study only Hindi and Sanskrit are 25% fewer than those who study only English and Hindi, while those who study only English and Sanskrit are 15 more than those who study all three. The total number of students who study English is 275, and the total who study Sanskrit is 220. All remaining students study only Hindi.
96-100.sol: None = 100, so 500 study at least one. All three 40; only E+H 60; only H+S 45; only E+S 55; only E 120; only S 80; only H 100.
